title: The nine-piece Reno band and Buster Smith's departure
summary: Clayton works out the nine-man Reno Club instrumentation and explains that Buster Smith had left for Texas, so Caughey Roberts was brought in.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: No, we didn't. Well see that was when we had, we only had, let me see now, we had three saxophones, three trumpets, golly we had more than, oh, we didn't have any trombones in the Reno.
: No, not a trombone?

No. We had three saxophones, three trumpets, Basie, Joe and Page, nine. That's the nine we had. So I could make arrangements for that. Though later when we came we added three trombones and another trumpet, another sax, two sax. I never remade it for a bigger band. We always went into something else. Yes, we didn't
like to cook old hash, you know what I mean?
That was, that must have had a very unusual sound, three trumpets and three saxes like that?
Yes.
Was Washington playing Baritone?
We did have a trombone. We had.....
I think it must have been .........
No, we had George Hunt. He was the only trombone. I'm trying to figure out how in the hell we had nine pieces. Jack Washington was there.
Well did you have three...
Oh!
Did you have three trumpets?

Yes, we had three trumpets. For a while there were eight pieces, we didn't have, there was only Jack Washington and Lester. Until we sent, see, because Prof, I don't know if you know Prof? Now I don't know his real name. He went to
Texas. He left Basie and went to Texas. That's why we had to call Caughey. You see, he left, he was a first man.
It wasn't Buster Smith?

Buster Smith, yes we call him Prof. Yes. You see, he went to Texas. So then we played with three trumpets, one trombone, that's four, two reeds, that's six and Page, Jo and Basie that's nine. That's the way it was when I came there. And later, I sent, we sent for Caughey and Herschel. They came in. But it was nine pieces when I first went there.
No lead alto man.
Buster Smith was a pretty good musician?
Right. Yes, he was.
But more of a lead than a soloist?
Well, I think so. In fact, he had gone when I got there.
So, from the way Basie talks and all the guys that he was missed very much when

he left. And it was like when Lips left, there was a vacancy that I took. But when Prof left, Buster, there was nobody to take it. And Basie was glad to get Coughy because on my recommendation, but Coughy still didn't quite fit into that kind of hard swinging band. He was a good musician. But Earle Coughy came along and fitted much better than Coughy did.
